module purpose: neorv32_uart keeps a control register that is written and read through the bus_req_i/bus_rsp_o record ports (enable, simulation mode, flow-control enable, prescaler select, baud divisor, five interrupt-condition enables, FIFO clear commands). Bytes written to its data address are queued in a TX FIFO sub-unit and shifted out bit-serially on uart_txd_o; bits sampled from uart_rxd_i are assembled into bytes and queued in an RX FIFO sub-unit for bus reads. It drives clkgen_en_o, uart_rtsn_o, irq_rx_o and irq_tx_o, and uart_ctsn_i can hold off transmission when flow control is enabled.

use-case flows.value: control settings (enable, simulation mode, flow-control enable, prescaler select, baud divisor, five interrupt-condition enables) taken from bus write data on a qualified write with address bit 2 = '0'
transmit byte from bus write data pushed into the TX FIFO sub-unit on a qualified write with address bit 2 = '1'
one-cycle FIFO clear commands and the resulting TX and RX FIFO flush decisions delivered to the FIFO sub-units
transmission: a byte popped from the TX FIFO, framed with a start bit, shifted out one bit per bit period (prescaler tick and baud countdown), started only when CTS permits under flow control
reception: the RX line synchronized, a start edge detected, bits sampled at half and full bit periods, the assembled byte written into the RX FIFO
RTS level computed from flow-control enable, UART enable and RX FIFO half status
in builds where sim_mode_en_c holds: data-register write bytes written to the simulation output instead of the TX FIFO path
RX and TX interrupt requests computed from interrupt-condition enables and FIFO status
receive overrun flag set when a received byte is written while the RX FIFO reports no free space
control settings, FIFO status, overrun and busy status, and the received byte (popped from the RX FIFO) returned on a qualified read
control register, response, interrupt outputs, both engines, overrun flag and RTS forced to constants while rstn_i = '0'
UART disable: both FIFOs flushed, overrun flag cleared, both engines held in their others branch

conceptual assets.concept: UART enable -- whether the transmitter, receiver, FIFOs, interrupt requests and clock-generator request are active
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configure flow: `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` (line 179) on a qualified control write (lines 176-178), cleared by reset (line 156). The module's behavior depends on the held value: '0' forces both FIFO flush decisions (lines 259, 304), clears bit 2 of tx_engine.state and bit 1 of rx_engine.state so both engines take their others branch (lines 344, 380-382, 417, 444-446), suppresses both interrupt requests (lines 270, 315), clears the overrun flag (lines 458-459) and drives uart_rtsn_o '1' under flow control (lines 472-475). Integrity is Established: a wrong value runs or halts these flows against the written setting. Availability is also Established: an unintended '0' flushes the FIFOs and stops transmission and reception. The value leaves the entity on clkgen_en_o (`clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable;`, line 228), whose consumer is not in this file, so the delivered value must equal the stored bit. ctrl.enable stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3; its GATES records target tx_fifo.clear, rx_fifo.clear, irq_tx_o, irq_rx_o, rx_engine.over and uart_rtsn_o); clkgen_en_o is the exit port (COPIES ctrl.enable, occurrence 2). bus_req_i.data, which supplies the bit, is a field of a transport record and is not a setting point. Line 195 returns the bit on any qualified read, so confidentiality is not established.

conceptual assets.concept: Simulation-mode setting -- whether both hardware FIFOs are held flushed and data-register writes are diverted to the simulation output
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configure flow: `ctrl.sim_mode <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_sim_en_c) and bool_to_ulogic_f(sim_mode_en_c);` (line 180). The setting can become '1' only in builds where sim_mode_en_c holds (line 50: SIM_MODE_EN and is_simulation_c, the latter from a package that is not supplied); in other builds line 180 keeps it '0', which is why the map lists it as a constant-valued CONTROL-ONLY source (its bus operand is recorded as GATES). In builds where the condition holds, '1' forces the TX and RX flush decisions every cycle (lines 259, 304, GATES tx_fifo.clear at occurrence 5), so neither engine receives data, and the simulation transmitter consumes data-register writes instead (line 499). Integrity is Established for those builds: a wrong value discards queued bytes and redirects transmit data against the written setting; availability of the hardware TX and RX paths depends on it as well. ctrl.sim_mode stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3).

conceptual assets.reasoning: Start, operate and read-out flows: the TX push is decided at line 261 (qualified write with address bit 2 = '1', GATED_BY bus_req_i.stb), the RX pop at line 307 (qualified read with address bit 2 = '1'), the TX pop at line 262 (tx_engine.state = 100) and the RX push by `rx_engine.done <= '1';` when the bit count reaches 0000 in state 11 (line 440, GATED_BY rx_engine.bitcnt), carried by `rx_fifo.we <= rx_engine.done;` (line 306). The four fields compute (GATED_BY at the cited occurrence). rx_engine.done has no qualifying use record for stores, so it is cited as the element that computes the push decision; rx_fifo.we is a combinational copy of it (COPIES rx_engine.done, line 306), so it is not listed even though line 460 tests it. bus_req_i.stb, rw and addr are fields of a transport record and are not setting points. tx_engine.done is assigned (lines 329, 340, 376) but has no driving record and is never read, so it realizes nothing here.
